blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: LLM agents often give conflicting answers to the same question, and many deployed agents are variants of one base model, so their errors are correlated. We study truth discovery among such agents: inferring the true answer and each agent's reliability without labels. Classical truth-discovery and crowdsourcing estimators reward an agreeing bloc and can fall below majority vote. We propose BP-TD, which adds per-agent decorrelation weights to mean-field variational inference on a one-coin Dawid-Skene model, so that agents sharing a base model count together as about one vote. Its first iteration is exactly a weighted vote; later iterations estimate agent reliability. With 13 local agents on MMLU, BP-TD beats majority vote without any labels (0.716 vs. 0.624 on 160 questions; 0.707 vs. 0.674 on 10,000) and ranks agents by their true accuracy, which classical estimators invert. The gain depends on the pool: over 2,852 sub-pools of four benchmarks, decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that tells the two cases apart. Labels change the picture quickly: with 20 labelled questions, selecting the single best agent is more accurate than every aggregator we tested on MMLU, ARC and TruthfulQA.

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en:
Ask the same factual question to several large language model (LLM)
agents and you will often get several different answers: on a
multiple-choice item, one model answers A, another B, a third abstains.
As LLM agents are wired together into pipelines, debates, and
mixtures, this disagreement is no longer a curiosity but an operational
problem—a system must commit to one answer, ideally the true
one, and ideally without paying for ground-truth labels at every step.
Deciding which answer to trust is exactly truth discovery (TD): a
data-quality problem with two decades of theory for conflicting Web
sources and crowd workers [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] .
Whether that theory transfers to AI agents, and when it does, has
not been characterized.

blocks.en:
The gap. Classical TD rests on a structural assumption:
sources are conditionally independent given the truth, so that
agreement is evidence of correctness and reliability can be estimated
from how often a source sides with the emerging consensus. This
assumption is routinely violated by AI agents for a reason specific to
them: deployed agents are frequently variants of the same base
model —prompt personas, self-consistency samples, or retrieval
wrappers around one LLM—so their errors are strongly correlated .
Reliability-by-agreement then rewards a correlated bloc that may be
confidently and unanimously wrong , and the standard TD machinery
inverts: it can rank the agreeing-but-wrong majority as most reliable.

blocks.en:
Classical truth discovery. A large body of work jointly estimates
source trust and claim belief by iterating between the two. Iterative
fixed-point methods include TruthFinder [ 1 ] and the
Investment and Sums/Hubs–Authorities schemes [ 6 ] ,
while CRH and CATD [ 3 ] cast the problem as joint
optimization with confidence-aware weighting; earlier fixed-point
corroboration [ 18 ] , correlation-aware
fusion [ 31 ] , and knowledge fusion over machine-extracted
triples [ 19 ] broaden the family (surveyed
in [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] ), and controlled evaluations find no estimator dominates
across source regimes [ 20 , 24 ] . These methods are unsupervised
and effective when sources err independently, but they provide no account of why a method should be expected to help on a given workload—the
regime question we make central.

a noisy annotator and infer a confusion structure: Dawid–Skene estimates
per-annotator error rates by EM [ 4 ] , and LTM extends this
with a generative Bayesian treatment of truth and reliability [ 5 ] ;

Belief propagation over the Dawid–Skene model is itself established and provably
optimal under independent annotators [ 13 ] ; our
contribution is the dependence-aware decorrelation layer that keeps inference
valid when annotators—here, agents—are correlated , which that line
does not address.
Our message-passing update reduces to a one-coin Dawid–Skene model when
agent weights are uniform; the contribution is not the latent-variable
machinery but the dependence-aware weighting layered on top of it.

Source dependence and copying. A key assumption of the above is
conditional independence of sources, which copying violates. Dong et
al. [ 2 ] detect copying among Web sources from shared false values and down-weight copied evidence, with global detection of
complex copying networks across many sources [ 30 ] ; in
crowdsourcing, spectral
and coupled-confusion methods handle correlated annotators beyond independent
Dawid–Skene [ 12 ] . Large-scale evidence confirms the
phenomenon directly for LLMs: higher-capability and same-provider models make correlated errors even across architectures [ 14 ] .
Our setting is the agent
analogue: agents that share a base model exhibit correlated errors by
construction. We adapt this intuition with family- and agreement-based
discounting so that a correlated bloc counts as roughly one effective vote,
and we show that a shared-error signal—the direct copy-detection
analogue—degrades when the dependent bloc is the majority.

What is new here. BP-TD builds on one-coin Dawid–Skene
inference [ 4 , 29 ] , discounting of dependent
sources [ 2 , 31 ] , and grouping of correlated
voters (our ClusterVote baseline). What differs with BP-TD is the dependence signal it
uses: provenance or raw answer co-occurrence,
never the current truth estimate, which we show is circular when the dependent bloc

inside a reliability model rather than collapsing each group to one hard vote; on

main empirical finding—decorrelation helps when the largest correlated bloc is
weaker than the other agents and hurts when it is the strongest—is not specific to
BP-TD: any rule that discounts a group of agreeing agents gives up that group’s votes,
which costs accuracy exactly when the group is right.

blocks.en:
The dependence problem. Classical truth discovery and the Dawid–Skene
model [ 4 ] assume agents are conditionally independent given the truth, so that agreement is evidence of correctness. This assumption is
violated for LLM ensembles: agents that share a base model, a prompt template, or
a retrieval corpus produce correlated errors , and a single such bloc can
manufacture a spurious majority. Our goal is therefore aggregation that down-weights dependent agents so a correlated bloc contributes roughly one effective vote.

blocks.en:
BP-TD combines (i) variational message passing on a one-coin Dawid–Skene factor

mean-field updates share this structure; the estimator itself is the mean-field one

blocks.en: VI-G When does agent truth discovery work?
blocks.zh: VI-G 级 特工发现真相什么时候起作用?

blocks.en:
The sub-pool study gives the practical rule: decorrelation helps when the agents that
agree most are not the agents that are most often right. Two further analyses refine it.

同意大多数不是最经常是正确的代理人。 另有两项分析加以完善。

blocks.en:
Disagreement. Within MMLU, the gain over majority vote grows with
per-question disagreement ( + 0.00 +0.00 , + 0.00 +0.00 , + 0.125 +0.125 , + 0.275 +0.275 across quartiles on one
held-out split; Fig. 5 ); within TruthfulQA it is never
positive; within SciQ it is flat. MMLU and TruthfulQA have nearly the same mean signed
agreement ( 0.33 0.33 and 0.35 0.35 ), so how much agents agree does not decide the outcome;

No label-free diagnostic. A practitioner needs to know which case applies

blocks.en: VII Discussion and Limitations
blocks.zh: 七. 讨论和限制

blocks.en:
What the gain means in practice. Consider a pipeline that answers 10,000 10{,}000 MMLU-style questions with these 13 13 agents and no labels. BP-TD family answers about 320 320 more questions correctly than majority vote ( 0.707 0.707 vs. 0.674 0.674 ) and reports
which agents are reliable; its one-pass form ( 0.702 0.702 ) runs in under a second on CPU. If the pool’s
largest group is its strongest, the same choice costs about 300 300 – 500 500 answers per 10,000 10{,}000 (median − 0.03 -0.03 to − 0.05 -0.05 on MMLU sub-pools). If 20 20 questions can be
labelled, choosing the best agent is better still: on the 160 160 -question MMLU sample
it reaches 0.805 0.805 , against 0.711 0.711 for BP-TD family. BP-TD is therefore a tool for the label-free case, for pools
in which redundant variants of a weak model would otherwise outvote stronger,
independent models, and for auditing agent reliability.

其单通式(0.702 0.702)在CPU上运行在一秒以内。 如果游泳池是
最大组群是其最强的组群,同样的选择成本大约为300-300-500分/万分/10{,}000分/(中位数-0.03-0.05-0.05分/MMLU子池). 如果20个问题
标注,选择最佳剂更好: 在160 160 - 问题 MMLU样本上
它达到了0.805 0.805,而BP-TD家庭为0.711 0.711。 因此,BP-TD是无标签案例、池的工具
在其中,一个弱型模型的冗余变体否则会胜过强势,
独立模型,用于审计代理人的可靠性。

blocks.en:
Limitations. (i) Benchmarks and scale. The regime results rest on four
benchmarks, of which only MMLU was harvested at scale; SciQ and TruthfulQA were not.
All agents are local open models of up to 14 14 B parameters; larger API-served models
were not tested and may be less redundant. (ii) Pool composition. The headline
gain depends on a pool whose largest group is weak (Sec. VI-C ). (iii) No
diagnostic. We found no label-free way to tell whether decorrelation will help.
(iv) Dependence model. The weights are a heuristic tempering of the likelihood,
not a generative model of dependence, and the truth-aware shared_error weights fail when the dependent bloc is the majority. (v) Contamination. The base
models have likely seen these benchmarks. Every aggregator receives the same answers,
so contamination does not favour one aggregator on a given answer matrix, but it can
change the answer matrix itself: if models of one family memorized the same items,
their errors are more shared, which is the variable our regime analysis depends on.
The TruthfulQA result in particular may partly reflect contamination rather than the
benchmark’s adversarial design alone.

blocks.en: VIII Conclusion
blocks.zh: 八 结论

blocks.en:
Truth discovery among LLM agents fails in its classical form because agents built on
one base model agree for reasons unrelated to the truth. Discounting such agents,
as BP-TD does with provenance or co-occurrence weights inside a Dawid–Skene model,
recovers a significant gain over majority vote on MMLU without labels, at 160 160 and
at 10,000 10{,}000 questions, and recovers the ranking of agents by accuracy where
classical estimators invert it. Its first iteration is a weighted vote; iteration
contributes the reliability estimates. Across thousands of sub-pools, the gain appears
when the largest correlated group is weaker than the other agents and reverses when
it is the strongest, and we found no label-free statistic that predicts which case
holds. With twenty labelled questions, choosing the best single agent is better than
every aggregator we tested. Two directions follow: a label-free test for the
direction of shared errors, and a rule for switching from aggregation to agent
selection as labels arrive.
